question: Why does the T1ce/WT SAM-Med3D arm plateau at ~0.57 DSC instead of the ~0.73-0.74 referenced from DPD-SAM?

protocol_alignment_with_dpdsam.verdict: ALIGNED on every dimension the paper discloses; the gap is NOT a task mismatch

target_definition.method: computed candidate label-set volume statistics over all 972 train cases and compared to DPD-SAM Table I
target_definition.conclusion: WT={1,2,3} with RC={4} excluded reproduces all three of DPD-SAM's reported statistics; every other definition is far off. Target definition is confirmed identical.

protocol_alignment_with_dpdsam.modality: DPD-SAM Sec. III: 'C = 1 for the T1ce sequence adopted in this work'. Identical to ours.
protocol_alignment_with_dpdsam.geometry: DPD-SAM: 'intensity normalization, bias field correction, and skull stripping ... resized to a consistent input dimension of 128x128x128'. Identical to our N4 whole-volume 128^3 cache.
protocol_alignment_with_dpdsam.loss: DPD-SAM Eq. 10 is Dice + BCE. Ours is generic.DiceCELoss(sigmoid=True, squared_pred=True).
protocol_alignment_with_dpdsam.augmentation: DPD-SAM: TorchIO random affine (rot 15 deg, transl 10%) + elastic + noise. Ours: train_augmentation='affine_elastic_noise'.
protocol_alignment_with_dpdsam.split_ratio: DPD-SAM: random 8:2 train/test on 1350 cases. Ours: outer 1080/270, i.e. the same 8:2, then an inner 972/108 so 108 cases are spent on validation that DPD-SAM does not spend.

hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: The mask decoder's output resolution caps achievable Dice
hypotheses_tested.measurement: image_encoder maps 128^3 -> 8^3x384 tokens; mask_decoder emits logits at 32^3, trilinearly upsampled 4x to 128^3. Naive emulation (downsample GT to 32^3, threshold 0.5, upsample) gives mean Dice 0.8105 over 1080 train+val cases.
hypotheses_tested.refutation: That 0.81 is an artifact of the 0.5 threshold. Optimizing a free 32^3 logit field per case by gradient descent against the 128^3 GT reaches mean Dice 0.9266 (median 0.9352) on the 108 validation cases; even the 'tiny' lesion bin reaches 0.8507. Continuous logits recover sub-grid boundary placement.
hypotheses_tested.verdict: REFUTED. Output resolution is not the binding constraint.

hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: WT is multi-focal, so a few point prompts cannot specify it
hypotheses_tested.measurement: connected components on validation WT: 43% of cases have >=2 components of >=50 voxels, but the largest component holds 99.8% of WT volume at the median, and only 12% of cases have <70% of volume in the largest component.
hypotheses_tested.verdict: REAL BUT MINOR. Multi-focality affects a minority of the volume.

hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: The 3-click budget is too small; DPD-SAM's baseline used a richer prompt
hypotheses_tested.measurement: validation-only diagnostic click-response curve on the frozen checkpoint: 1 click 0.5432, 3 clicks 0.5633, 5 clicks (SAM-Med3D official budget) 0.5731, 10 clicks 0.5821.
hypotheses_tested.verdict: REFUTED. Ten accumulated GT-derived corrective clicks buy only +0.039 over one. Even at the official 5-click budget the arm reads 0.573, nowhere near 0.741. The interaction channel is nearly saturated, i.e. the model behaves as a prompt-insensitive semantic segmenter.

hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: The model systematically over- or under-segments
hypotheses_tested.measurement: test click 3: precision 0.5618, recall 0.6152, median predicted/GT volume ratio 1.103. Balanced.
hypotheses_tested.verdict: REFUTED for the aggregate. Errors are boundary/extent errors, not a volume bias. Exception: the tiny-lesion bin over-predicts 2.63x, consistent with the model having learned an average lesion scale.

hypotheses_tested.hypothesis: The architecture plus the 3-click protocol cannot represent this task
hypotheses_tested.measurement: capacity probe: same model, same full unfreeze, same LRs (1e-4/1e-5), same 3-click cumulative forward, augmentation DISABLED, trained on a fixed 48-case subset of the 972. Fit Dice on those same 48 cases: epoch 10 = 0.7748, epoch 20 = 0.8267, epoch 40 = 0.8627, epoch 60 = 0.8803, epoch 80 = 0.8846 (final, 80/80 epochs, 918 s). Plateaued from epoch ~60: the last 20 epochs move fit Dice by +0.004.
hypotheses_tested.verdict: REFUTED, decisively. The architecture reaches 0.88 and passes the 0.741 reference by epoch ~9 when it does not have to generalize.

diagnosis.primary: GENERALIZATION GAP, not capacity, resolution, target definition, prompt budget, or preprocessing.
evidence: Capacity probe fits 48 unaugmented cases to 0.88; the arm's validation is stuck at 0.5677.
Arm history: train Dice rises 0.398 -> 0.685 across 64 epochs while val Dice plateaus from epoch ~12 and best-argmax lands at epoch 24 (0.5677). 40 further epochs never beat it.
Train-minus-validation Dice gap widens to ~0.11 even with affine+elastic+noise augmentation active.
100,509,232 parameters fully unfrozen against 972 training scans (613 subjects, ~1.6 scans/subject) is a very high parameter-to-sample ratio.

secondary.finding: Performance is dominated by lesion size
secondary.implication: The large-lesion third already reads 0.698. If the 95 sub-8000-voxel cases (35% of the test set) matched large-case performance, the scan-macro mean would be 0.642. Small-lesion behaviour, not average behaviour, is what separates 0.57 from 0.70.

reference_credibility.note: Recorded as context, not as an excuse. The protocol alignment above means the gap is real under a like-for-like task definition.
observations: DPD-SAM Table III reports mean+-std over 5 runs. SAM-Med3D 74.1+-1.5; nnU-Net 72.8+-1.2; plain U-Net 51.9+-2.1; 2D SAM ViT-B 68.4 on 3D post-operative MRI (Table IV).
BCGFMamba transcribes the same SAM-Med3D number as 73.1, which does not match DPD-SAM's own table.

DPD-SAM states SAM-based baselines use 'automatically generated prompts under a unified protocol without any manual boxes or points'; the actual prompt construction for the SAM-Med3D row is never specified.
DPD-SAM's own 86.8 is produced by a diffusion refinement U-Net operating at full 128^3 on top of the SAM mask (Table II), i.e. its headline number does not come from the SAM decoder at all.

geometry_vs_nnunet_style_pipeline.prompted_by: Operator asked on 2026-08-06 whether this project skips preprocessing, comparing against a colleague's U-Mamba pipeline: binarize -> crop to nonzero -> resample to 1mm -> brain z-score -> random 128x160x112 patches.

step_by_step.crop_to_nonzero: WE DO NOT. This is a real gap. We resize the whole volume to 128^3.
step_by_step.resample_to_1mm: NO-OP for BraTS 2024. Measured median voxel zoom over 120 train cases is [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] and median shape 182x218x182 (SRI atlas space); the data is already 1mm isotropic.
step_by_step.brain_zscore: WE DO. 'source nonzero-voxel population z-score before resize'.
step_by_step.random_patch_128x160x112: WE DO NOT, and CANNOT without changing the architecture: SAM-Med3D vit_b_ori uses a 16^3 PatchEmbed3D with positional embeddings fixed to an 8^3 token grid, i.e. the input shape is pinned to 128^3.
step_by_step.extra_step_we_add: N4 bias field correction (SimpleITK, 4x50, shrink 2), which the colleague's pipeline does not list.

measured_cost_of_skipping_crop_to_nonzer.interpretation: Cropping to the brain bounding box before the 128^3 resize roughly doubles the lesion's voxel count on the model grid and lifts the native-space reconstruction ceiling from 0.930 to 0.968. The gain is largest exactly in the small-lesion bin (0.876 -> 0.952), which is this arm's diagnosed weak regime.

metric_space_caveat.statement: Our reported DSC compares prediction and GT both on the 128^3 model grid. An nnU-Net/U-Mamba pipeline restores its prediction to the native 1mm grid and scores there. Two DSC values on different spatial grids (DSC itself is dimensionless).

measured_not_estimated.method: Re-ran the frozen checkpoint on all 108 validation cases, restored each click-3 prediction to the native 182x218x182 @1mm grid with nearest-exact, and re-scored against the untouched GT NIfTI.
measured_not_estimated.self_check: the 128^3 column reproduced the published validation readout 0.5633 exactly

metric_space_caveat.correction: An earlier claim in this project's chat that native-space re-scoring would cost ~0.03 (0.571 -> ~0.54-0.55) was derived by multiplying the readout by the 0.923 GT ceiling. That multiplication is invalid and the measurement refutes it: the true cost is 0.0014. The 0.923 ceiling binds a PERFECT prediction; at 0.56 accuracy the model's own regional errors dominate and almost entirely absorb the extra resampling error.
metric_space_caveat.consequence: The metric-space difference is negligible at the current accuracy level, so comparison against a native-resolution pipeline is essentially fair as-is and cannot be used to explain the shortfall in either direction. The 0.923 ceiling would only start to bind above roughly 0.85 DSC.

token_budget_waste.consequence: About 52% of our 128^3 input lies outside the brain bounding box and ~79% of its voxels are literally zero. Of the image encoder's 8^3 = 512 tokens, roughly 267 cover mostly background. This, not the metric space, is the real cost of skipping crop-to-nonzero: it is a wasted-capacity argument about the input, not a measurement argument about the score.

crop_to_nonzero_probe_20260806.question: Does inserting crop-to-nonzero before the 128^3 resize help, using the ALREADY-TRAINED whole-head weights?
crop_to_nonzero_probe_20260806.design: 2x2: {epoch 24 best, epoch 64 latest} x {whole-head resize, crop-to-nonzero then resize}. Only the geometry changes. N4 (shrink 2), the nonzero-population z-score, the 3-click cumulative protocol, seed 20260723 and the weights are identical. The z-score is provably unaffected by the crop: it is taken over the nonzero-voxel population and cropping to the nonzero bounding box does not change which voxels are nonzero.
crop_to_nonzero_probe_20260806.scoring: every cell restored to the native 182x218x182 @1mm grid and compared against the untouched GT NIfTI, so all four numbers sit on the same grid
crop_to_nonzero_probe_20260806.split: validation 108 only; NO test data read
crop_to_nonzero_probe_20260806.prediction_that_was_wrong: Before running this, the agent predicted that feeding brain-cropped input to whole-head-trained weights would be a train/eval preprocessing mismatch and would LOWER the score, so the probe could not demonstrate any benefit. That prediction is refuted: the effect is positive, and for epoch 64 it is statistically clear (95% CI excludes zero, sign test p=0.00068). The operator's original instinct to test the geometry directly was better than the agent's objection.
honest_limits: The epoch-24 effect is NOT significant (CI spans zero, p=0.63). Only the epoch-64 effect is.
The agent has no confident explanation for why epoch 64 benefits (+0.0274) far more than epoch 24 (+0.0040). Stated as an observation, not a mechanism.
This is still a mismatched-input measurement. It is a LOWER bound on what training with the crop would give, not an estimate of it.

n=108. The best cell (epoch64 + brain_crop = 0.5712) beats the frozen configuration (epoch24 + whole_head = 0.5619), but picking it is a validation-based selection and would need a fresh freeze before any test readout.
crop_to_nonzero_probe_20260806.conclusion: crop-to-nonzero is confirmed worth training with. It is a real, cheap, single-factor gain even before retraining.

implications_for_next_arm: Levers that address the generalization gap: train on the full 1080 outer-train (subject-clean CV instead of a fixed 108 holdout); stronger/longer augmentation; partial rather than full unfreeze, or layer-wise LR decay; EMA of weights; early-stopping already fires very early so the epoch budget is not the constraint.

Levers that address the size dependence: size-stratified or size-reweighted sampling; a loss less dominated by large lesions than mean Dice; a two-stage coarse-to-fine crop so small lesions are not resolved at whole-head scale.
The single structural difference from DPD-SAM's pipeline that remains untested is its full-resolution refinement stage operating on the SAM mask at 128^3.
None of the above may be selected using the 270-case test. Model development returns to the 972/108 clean validation.
test_access: This record consumed NO new test data. Per-case numbers quoted for the 270 cases were read from the already-published FROZEN_TEST270_FULLUNFREEZE_20260805.json report, not by re-running the evaluator. All new computation ran on the 972 train and 108 validation splits.
